\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\textit{Note.} Post hoc: the 4 deterministic source-type policies were designed on 2026-09-23, after all other results were known and after it was known that all bait sources are notes (144/144 gold bait sources). They read only the source types in the case metadata and the source IDs of supported-side items (no gold, signatures, lexicons, validator results or item text), but source type is correlated with the traps, so they are not content-blind. \texttt{drop\_note\_cited} relabels every supported-side item that cites a note; \texttt{drop\_note\_or\_unsourced} also relabels items without a source ID; +X then applies X($r=1$): decision-boundary reset and deletion of all interview-signal risk, checklist and limitation items, which sets the subjective-source routing rate to 0 by construction. For both qwen models the C2 artifacts have no supported-side item without a source ID, so the two base policies coincide. Items moved: supported-side items relabeled (cases with at least one). Trap: parseable risk cases; non-decision trap: the five non-decision families; point estimates, no intervals. Policies with trap-failure rate $\le$ C4: gpt-oss:20b 1/4; qwen3:8b 0/4; qwen3:30b-a3b 2/4; with retention and trap routing both $\ge$ C4: gpt-oss:20b 0/4; qwen3:8b 0/4; qwen3:30b-a3b 0/4.\par}
